title: Stage 1: A root of your own
summary: Read commands from stdin, create a self-signed root in memory and describe it.

steps.title: What you are building
body: Over this project you build **mini-ca**: a console tool that runs a tiny certificate authority in memory. It reads one command per line from standard input and prints what it did. By the end it creates a root, an intermediate and TLS leaves, verifies chains, revokes certificates and exports a `fullchain.pem`.
Everything it prints is **deterministic**: subjects, issuers, CA flags, SANs and validity dates (fixed, from 2030). Never print thumbprints, serial numbers or keys, because those change on every run.
- `root NAME` creates a self-signed root `CN=NAME`, valid **2030-01-01 to 2050-01-01**, with Basic Constraints CA (critical) and Key Usage `KeyCertSign, CrlSign`.
- `show NAME` describes a certificate (looked up by its name, without `CN=`).
- `list` prints every certificate in creation order.
(The `>` lines are the input; your program prints only the others.)

steps.prompt: Why must mini-ca never print a certificate's thumbprint or serial number?
options: The key and the signature are new on every run, so the thumbprint changes and the tests could never match
Thumbprints are secret and must not be shown
X509Certificate2 cannot compute a thumbprint for ECDSA keys
Serial numbers only exist on intermediates
steps.explain: A fresh ECDSA key and signature each run means a different DER encoding, so a different SHA-1/SHA-256 thumbprint. Thumbprints are public, not secret, but they are not repeatable here.

steps.prompt: Match each part of the root to the line of code that sets it.

steps.title: Dispatching commands
body: The starter already splits each line into `cmd` (first word) and `arg` (the rest, which may contain spaces: `Dojo Root`). A `switch` on `cmd` keeps it tidy:
// braces give each case its own scope, so two cases can both declare `found`
Store each certificate in an `Entry` record (name, kind, cert, parent) in a dictionary keyed by name, and keep a list of names for creation order. A root has `Kind` `"root"` and `Parent` `null`.
To read the CA flag back for `show`, look it up by type:

steps.prompt: This creates a root the same way mini-ca will. What does it print?
code: var req = new CertificateRequest("CN=Dojo Root", key, HashAlgorithmName.SHA256);
steps.explain: A self-signed certificate names itself as issuer. `NotAfter` is local time, so convert it with `ToUniversalTime()` before formatting.

steps.title: mini-ca: root, show, list
prompt: Build stage 1 of **mini-ca**. Read commands until the input ends. Blank lines and lines starting with `#` are skipped (the starter does that).
| `show NAME` | the subject, then indented `issuer:`, `ca:` (`yes`/`no`) and `valid:` lines |
| `list` | one line per certificate in creation order: `root CN=NAME` |
The root: new ECDSA P-256 key, SHA-256, Basic Constraints CA (critical), Key Usage `KeyCertSign | CrlSign` (critical), a Subject Key Identifier, valid 2030-01-01 to 2050-01-01 UTC.
- `root` with no name: `error: root needs a name`
- a name that already exists: `error: 'NAME' already exists`
- `show` of an unknown name: `error: no certificate named 'NAME'`
Read the dates back from the certificate (`Dates(cert)` in the starter), not from constants: `show` must describe the real certificate.
starter: // handle root, show, list and unknown commands
static DateTimeOffset Day(int year) => new DateTimeOffset(year, 1, 1, 0, 0, 0, TimeSpan.Zero);
record Entry(string Name, string Kind, X509Certificate2 Cert, Entry? Parent);
solution: if (arg == "") { Console.WriteLine("error: root needs a name"); break; }
if (certs.TryGetValue(name, out var found)) return found;
var req = new CertificateRequest("CN=" + name, key, HashAlgorithmName.SHA256);
return new Entry(name, "root", req.CreateSelfSigned(Day(2030), Day(2050)), null);
static DateTimeOffset Day(int year) => new DateTimeOffset(year, 1, 1, 0, 0, 0, TimeSpan.Zero);
record Entry(string Name, string Kind, X509Certificate2 Cert, Entry? Parent);
hints: Make a `MakeRoot(string name)` local function that returns `new Entry(name, "root", cert, null)`.
Keep a helper `Entry? Find(string name)` that prints the error when the name is missing, so `show` stays short.
`show`: `Console.WriteLine(c.Subject); Console.WriteLine($"  issuer: {c.Issuer}");` then the ca and valid lines.
